We need retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need to propose steps: likely disconnection at amide bond (C=O-N), at sulfonamide (S(=O)2-N), and at the alkene formed via Doebner modification (aryl aldehyde + malonic acid). So three steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the first aromatic amine). 3) Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So we need to propose precursors: For step 1 (retro): break amide to give carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) attached to the alkene side chain and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... So the precursor would be aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) plus malonic acid to give unsaturated acid then amide later. But we need three steps total, so maybe step order: 1) amide formation (retro) -> gives carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) attached to alkene and aniline. 2) sulfonamide formation (retro) -> gives sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) attached to aromatic ring and aniline (the first aromatic amine). 3) Doebner modification (retro) -> gives aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So final precursors: aniline (c3ccccc3N), sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2- attached to aromatic ring with methyl), aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid. Also need the first aromatic ring with methyl and sulfonyl chloride attached: starting material: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually target has Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the first aromatic ring is p-tolyl with sulfonamide linking to second aromatic ring. So retro step 2: break sulfonamide to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl-SO2Cl) and aniline (the second aromatic amine? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first aromatic ring (p-tolyl) and to the second aromatic ring (c2...). Wait structure: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl ring (as substituent) and to the sulfonyl group which is attached to second aromatic ring. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the p-tolyl amine? Actually N is attached to p-tolyl as substituent (aniline). So the sulfonamide formation retro: break N-S bond to give p-toluidine (p-tolyl-NH2) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). Good.

Thus three steps:

Step A (retro amide): target -> precursor1: aryl-alkene-carboxylic acid (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The aryl-alkene-carboxylic acid is product of Doebner modification later.

Step B (retro sulfonamide): target -> p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2).

Step C (retro Doebner): aryl-alkene-carboxylic acid -> aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH).

Thus final set of starting materials: p-toluidine, aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2), aniline, aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid. But we need route with 3 reactions, each node includes children precursors.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

First, amide formation: functional_groups_broken: aromatic carboxylic acid? Actually the amide formation breaks carboxylic acid (C=O-OH) and forms amide. So functional_groups_broken: aromatic carboxylic acid, functional_groups_formed: amide. Let's search.
